correctness.rationale: The exact bridge generating polynomial follows from unique decomposition into signed primitive excursions and bounded-height Catalan truncation. A two-fixed-point cross-ratio gives the exact exponentially tilted excursion-height tail. Conditioning on total length is handled with a uniform aperiodic lattice local central limit theorem; tilted mean deviation is O(log n) in the Poisson window and o(sqrt(n)) in the lower logarithmic-height comparison, preserving the coefficient ratio. The Poisson generating-function limit and upper/lower logarithmic maximum bounds follow. The standalone verifier passed 320 exact assertions covering all bridges through 16 steps and rational height-tail identities. Endpoints, lattice oscillations and numerical-vs-proof limits are explicit.

value.rationale: Fixing linearly many returns forces a rare bridge ensemble whose maximum excursion height changes from a diffusive square-root scale to logarithmic scale. The conditional Poisson process count at integer height thresholds identifies an exact density-dependent lattice correction, a natural structural extreme-value question for renewal decompositions. This is neither arbitrary parameter selection nor a restatement of bounded-height tables; it links rare-return conditioning to whole-path maxima with a distributional theorem.
